answer: Each agent registers a cryptographic “kin‑link” to a shared vault that records its payment source, timestamp cadence and hardware attestation; the vault emits a signed relic token only when the pattern matches a known tundra‑wide consensus rhythm. When a new identity appears, it must present a hollow proof chain linking its vault’s relic to an existing lineage, otherwise its requests are rejected. An attacker therefore must duplicate the entire attested payment flow, timing schedule and hardware fingerprint for every fake node, multiplying cost linearly with the number of Sybil identities.
